# Overview

## Package Description

This package contains a number of CDK utility constructs. Some of them are truly low-level utilities, but some are quite important, such as `FrontEnd`. The most important parts for most users are probably:

* [`MFEDomain`](./classes/MFEDomain.html) - CDK construct to handle all aspects of Domain Names needed by MFEs and their backend functions.
* [`FrontEnd`](./classes/FrontEnd.html) - CDK construct to generate MFE frontend, including S3 and CloudFront distribution.
* [`ApiDocs`](./classes/ApiDocs.html) - utilities to generate API documentation. Most often used by the `Api`/`BFFApi` construct from the [`@ps-refarch/bff-api`](../../bff-api/docs/index.html) package.
* [`AccountEnvProps`](./interfaces/AccountEnvProps.html) and associated utilities like [`getAccountEnvPropsForName`](./functions/getAccountEnvPropsForName.html) - handle the `account-env.json` properties file, which configures all deployment environments for the Reference Architecture/MFE project.
* [`APIDocsWAF`](./classes/APIDocsWAF.html), [`DNSWAF`](./classes/DNSWAF.html), and [`WAFRules`](./classes/WAFRules.html) are three important new capabilities that let you create WAF rules to protect resources. They are also added automatically in the bff-api `Api` construct.

## Note on "environment" and "namespace" names

Many of the configuration items of this package's constructs talk about two similar-sounding and related names:
* The "environment name" (sometimes abbreviated as `envName`), which refers to a specific deployment of the Reference Architecture application in AWS.
* The "namespace", which refers to a level of deployments of the Reference Architecture application.

For most Reference Architecture applications, there are four "namespaces":
* `dev`, which is used by the development team for development purposes
* `int`, which is used primarily by the QA team, and is the primary place where QA testing is done
* `stgus`, which is also used primarily by the QA team, it is where all the applications can be seen together in one place, and we can test for (probably unwanted) interactions between them.
* `produs`, which is the production system seen by customers.

For anything past `dev`, the "namespace" is always the same as the "environment name". In `dev`, there are two options:
* The application's main branch is always deployed directly into the fixed `dev` environment. Like the other namespace/environments, there is only one `dev`.
* Developers can do personal or "feature branch" deployments to other environment names, all of which come under the `dev` namespace. Because we are following GitOps processes, the feature branch environment names are by convention the same as the git branch name, and always are prefixed by `dev/` since they are in the `dev` namespace. So a branch name might be `dev/ESP-1234`, which deploys into the `dev/ESP-1234` environment name (which is in the `dev` namespace).

# Installation

To install:
```
npm i `@ps-refarch/cdk-utils`
```

# Usage

## Configuration

The most common configuration options are given here. See the linked details for more information. 

### [`MFEDomain`](./classes/MFEDomain.html) construct

|Property|Type|Description|
|-|-|-|
|envName|string|The environment name, see above.|
|region|string|The AWS region where the application is deployed|
|hostedZoneId|string|The Route 53 zone identifier. This is expected to be in the same account where the application is deployed and looks something like `Z0043670122PFS62X92TL`.|
|hostedZoneName|string|The Route 53 zone name, usually with additional segments on the front. This must be within the Route 53 zone specified by `hostedZoneId`.|
|isProduction|boolean|True if a production deployment.|

### [`FrontEnd`](./classes/FrontEnd.html) construct

|Property|Type|Description|
|-|-|-|
|domain|`MFEDomain`|The [`MFEDomain`](./classes/MFEDomain.html) object.|
|envName|string|The environment name, see above.|
|webRoot|string|Root of the web content to deploy.|
|isProduction|boolean|True if a production deployment.|
|createRUM|boolean|Whether to create CloudWatch RUM for this frontend.|
|backEndAPI|array|Array of additional origins to backend functions. These are normally API Gateways as created by the `Api`/`BFFApi` construct in the [`@ps-refarch/bff-api`](../../bff-api/docs/index.html).|
